body.x: Capturing a physical object in 3D, reviewing it with colleagues and presenting it to customers typically means moving between separate tools and devices.
A single workflow that runs from an iPhone scan to a shared session on Apple Vision Pro is the gap dilium aims to close.

dilium srl, an Italian spatial computing company founded in 2017 and led by CEO Donato De Ieso, develops immersive technologies that make 3D content practical for business, education, product presentation and technical collaboration. Its core product, 3DtoMe, lets users capture physical objects with an iPhone or Mac, create digital twins, review them in a web browser, and add annotations and measurements. The same content works across compatible devices, including Apple Vision Pro. At KES 2026, dilium is exhibiting 3DtoMe - Spatial 3D Studio, which won a KES 2026 Innovation Award in the XR & Spatial Computing category.

dilium combines computer vision, LiDAR, object capture, real-time 3D rendering and AI to build accessible, interoperable 3D workflows. 3DtoMe connects creation, review, presentation and real-time spatial collaboration in one cross-device workflow. Visitors to the booth can try precise annotation with Logitech Muse, along with physical control and spatial anchoring through seeMote Cube.

dilium has completed more than 30 projects, won more than 6 tenders and reached more than 2 million views and uses across its applications, and it serves more than 3,000 customers worldwide. In 2023, Apple selected the company for its Apple Vision Pro Developer Labs in London and Cupertino, and by 2026 dilium had launched 6 applications for Apple Vision Pro. Its technologies have been presented internationally through Italian Trade Agency delegations at WAICF Cannes and MWC Barcelona.

As a software company, dilium does not export physical products. It delivers 3DtoMe, Spatial Plan, Spatial Companion and its other applications through the Apple App Store, Apple Business Manager and web-based platforms, so users outside Italy can adopt them without local physical distribution.

dilium plans to expand 3DtoMe and its wider spatial computing ecosystem in South Korea and other Asian markets through enterprise pilot projects, local technology partnerships and product localization. Development will focus on cross-device 3D collaboration, digital-twin workflows, spatial AI, and integrations with enterprise systems and emerging spatial hardware.

The company names South Korea a priority market because its electronics, advanced manufacturing, design and digital-content industries suit digital twins and collaborative 3D workflows. At the show, dilium aims to meet Korean enterprises, technology partners and organizations exploring spatial computing. It is looking for local system integrators, Apple ecosystem partners, XR and spatial computing specialists, and enterprise partners that can develop pilot projects and provide technical support.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
